method: Six real child-process invocations of experiments/phase2-cpu-seg-v1/runner.py with G:\Anaconda\python.exe, driven by a psutil-watching wrapper that sampled peak_wset every 10 ms. Wall time is measured around the whole process, so it includes the torch import (the training segment alone is reported by the runner as rawWallTimeMs).
driverScript: Ephemeral measurement driver (not distributed; machine-local path omitted)

derivation.perAttemptTimeoutMsReason: Observed worst case is 3208 ms wall for a 5-step ab run including torch import. 120000 ms is 37x that, which leaves room for a cold filesystem and an antivirus scan without allowing an unbounded run. It matches the timeout the existing LightweightRunner integration test already uses.
derivation.maxMemoryBytesReason: Observed worst-case peak working set is 611389440 bytes (583 MiB) for a 3-module-capable run. 4 GiB is ~7x that; a module that allocates an unbounded intermediate fails the budget rather than the machine.
derivation.maxDiskBytesReason: Observed worst-case per-run output directory is 3615 bytes. 2 GiB is a generous ceiling that still bounds an accidental artifact explosion; the real disk cost is dominated by artifacts/runs and work/research-execution, not by these files.
derivation.maxExecutionSecondsReason: A full smoke sweep is at most 4 variants x 1 seed x 3.3 s ~= 13 s, and a tiny sweep at most 5 variants x 2 seeds x 3.3 s ~= 33 s. 300 s covers a smoke plus a tiny plus process overhead with margin, and is the value the freeze checklist already proposed.
derivation.maxTrialsReason: Largest declared sweep in this profile is 5 variants (baseline,a,b,ab,abc) x 2 seeds = 10 runs, so the budget must allow at least 10 to not be a lie. 8 was the freeze-checklist placeholder and would under-provision the abc tiny sweep; 12 is set instead: 5 x 2 = 10 runs plus 2 retries of a transient failure. See budget.maxTrials.

honesty: These numbers are from THIS machine (Windows 11, Intel64 Family 6 Model 151, RTX 4070 SUPER host, torch 2.9.1+cu126 CPU path) and are not a cross-machine claim.
The cold-start cost is dominated by importing torch (~3.1 s of the ~3.2 s wall). A warm filesystem may be faster; nothing here assumes that.
